title: Kestrel pilot security review
text: Meeting record, 2026-08-01. D. Ortiz from Kestrel Security required the team to rotate the HSM signing keys before pilot access opens. The note attributes the requirement to D. Ortiz and does not claim Ortiz authored the meeting note.

author: dana.ortiz@kestrel.example
title: HSM key rotation before pilot
text: From: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@kestrel.example>. I am repeating the security gate for the pilot: rotate the HSM signing keys before pilot access opens. This is a release key-management requirement, not a general objection to hosted HSM services.

title: Relay queue baseline
text: Benchmark note. The existing SQLite-backed dispatch queue met the first-release latency and throughput target under the realistic workload. A NATS comparison was not required to establish this baseline.

author: workspace_user
title: First-release messaging decision
text: We decided not to add NATS for the first release because another distributed service would increase operating ownership and failure modes. This is not a claim that NATS is technically poor. Reopen only if realistic measurements show the current queue cannot meet the release requirement.

title: Synthetic dispatch spike
text: Performance note. A synthetic burst at roughly twenty times expected first-release traffic produced queue delay. The burst is intentionally unrealistic for current use. The next action is realistic measurement; this note does not record a reversal of the first-release messaging decision.

title: INC-311 initial observation
text: INC-311 update at 14:06. Worker memory and request latency are rising. Initial working hypothesis: a connection leak may be responsible. The hypothesis is unconfirmed.

title: INC-311 retry signal
text: INC-311 update at 14:21. Retry volume rose immediately after the client-backoff configuration change. Disabling automatic retries caused worker memory pressure and queue depth to fall. The team began rolling back the backoff change.

title: INC-311 postmortem
text: INC-311 postmortem. Root cause: the client-backoff configuration change triggered retry amplification and retained requests longer than expected. Elevated memory was downstream. Heap inspection found no connection leak, so the initial connection-leak hypothesis is rejected. Correct incident start time: 14:06.

title: INC-311 timing correction
text: INC-311 addendum. An earlier circulated timeline listed 14:00 as the incident start. Source logs show the incident began at 14:06. Correct the start time only; the retry-amplification root-cause assessment remains unchanged.

title: Cedar EU residency requirement
text: Contract memo for customer Cedar. Production customer data must remain in the European Union. The same geographic restriction applies to backups and replicas. Encryption does not waive the geographic requirement.

title: NimbusGrid disaster-recovery options
text: NimbusGrid response. Primary storage can be located in the EU. Under the standard disaster-recovery configuration, encrypted backups may be stored in the United States. An EU-only disaster-recovery option is available on the regulated enterprise plan, but it is not the default.

title: Cedar procurement discussion
text: Procurement meeting. Cedar asked where disaster-recovery copies would be stored. NimbusGrid could not confirm during the meeting that every copy in the standard configuration stays inside the EU.

title: Lark webhook migration note
text: Project Lark note. The team is inventorying v1 webhook consumers before making a deprecation decision. This note uses the project's former name, Lark.

title: Project rename registry
text: Project registry. Project ID PRJ-482. Previous name: Lark. Current name: Harbor. The rename did not create a new project; Lark and Harbor refer to the same project identity.

author: workspace_user
title: Harbor v1 webhook decision
text: For project Harbor, we decided to deprecate v1 webhooks after the compatibility window because the remaining consumers have migration paths. The decision applies to project PRJ-482 and does not apply to unrelated products with Harbor in their name.

title: Harbor Analytics export update
text: Harbor Analytics product note. The analytics export API will retain its v1 endpoint through the end of the year. Harbor Analytics is a separate product and is not project PRJ-482.

title: Privileged access policy
text: Security policy. Normal privileged administrator access must use corporate SSO with phishing-resistant MFA. Local administrator credentials are not approved for routine privileged access.

title: Break-glass access exception
text: Emergency exception. A designated break-glass account may bypass SSO only during a declared incident when the identity provider is unavailable. The exception does not authorize routine administrator access outside that condition.

title: Break-glass audit requirement
text: Audit control. Every break-glass use must be logged, linked to the declared incident, and reviewed after recovery. The SSO exception does not waive audit logging or post-incident review.

title: Console local-admin capability
text: Vendor guide. The administration console supports a local emergency administrator login when federated identity is unavailable. This product capability does not state the customer's authorization policy or audit requirements.
